read.sections.0.text.note: "Thu phóng" is chosen as the glossary word for zoom (it is used for zooming a map or camera). "quy mô hẹp / quy mô rộng" for close and wide scale. Please check that "quy mô hẹp" and "quy mô rộng" are natural, and that "thu phóng" is understood by a 12-year-old.
read.sections.0.text.source: On a map on a screen, you can zoom in to see one street or zoom out to see a whole country. Historians do something similar with the past, because they choose a scale. Scale means how big a piece of time, place or group you decide to study. A close scale looks at one day, one letter or one family. A wide scale might follow a whole town for 100 years, or compare many regions over thousands of years. Look at Riverstone. At the scale of one afternoon, the story is about rain and a closed bridge. Over 20 years, it is about a town that grows. Over several hundred years, it is about a river that moves.
read.sections.0.text.back: On a map on a screen, you can zoom: zoom in to see a street or zoom out to see a whole country. Historians do the same thing with the past, because they choose a scale. Scale is how wide or narrow the stretch of time, place or group of people is that you choose to study. A narrow scale looks at one day, one letter or one family. A wide scale can follow a whole town over 100 years, or compare many regions over thousands of years. Look at Riverstone. At the scale of one afternoon, the story is about the rain and a closed bridge. Over 20 years, it is the story of a growing town. Over a few hundred years, it is the story of a river changing place.

read.sections.0.simpler.note: "Thu phóng" and "quy mô" stay as glossary words. "Hàng trăm năm" for "hundreds of years". Check.
read.sections.0.simpler.source: On a map, you can zoom in and out. Historians do this with the past too. They choose a scale. Scale means how much time or place you look at. A close scale is one day or one family. A wide scale is a town over 100 years. In Riverstone, the story of one afternoon is about rain and a bridge. Over 20 years, the town grows. Over hundreds of years, the river moves.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: On a map, you can zoom. Historians do the same with the past. They choose a scale. Scale is how much time or how much place you look at. A narrow scale is one day or one family. A wide scale is a town over 100 years. In Riverstone, the story of one afternoon is about rain and a bridge. Over 20 years, the town grows. Over hundreds of years, the river changes place.

read.sections.1.heading.note: "Cận cảnh" for the close view (borrowed from film and photography). Check it is understood.

read.sections.1.text.note: "Cận cảnh" for "a close view" and "toàn cảnh" for "a wide view". They are the translator's choice; no KEY_TERMS entry.
read.sections.1.text.source: A close view helps us notice people's choices, feelings and small details. A diary, a receipt or one photograph can show how an event changed one person's day. For example, a trader's diary might say that she waited six hours for the bridge to open. However, one person's day is not always the same as everyone else's. Other traders may have taken the long road instead. So close evidence needs context, which means we need to know what was happening around it at the time.
read.sections.1.text.back: A close-up helps us notice people's choices, feelings and small details. A diary, a receipt or a photo can show how an event changed one person's day that day. For example, a merchant's diary might record that she waited six hours for the bridge to reopen. However, one person's day is not always the same as everyone else's day. Other merchants might have taken a detour. So close-up evidence needs context, meaning we need to know what else was going on around it at that time.

read.sections.1.simpler.source: A close view shows people. We see their choices and feelings. A diary or a receipt shows one person's day. A trader may wait six hours for the bridge. But other traders may take the long road. One person's day is not everyone's day. So we need context. Context is what is going on around the source.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: A close-up shows people. We see their choices and feelings. A diary or a receipt shows one person's day. A merchant might have to wait six hours for the bridge. But other merchants might take a detour. One person's day is not everyone's day. So we need context. Context is what is going on around that source.

read.sections.2.heading.note: "Toàn cảnh" for wide view. Check; alternative "cái nhìn rộng".

read.sections.2.text.note: "Mẫu hình" for pattern (KEY_TERMS; alternative "quy luật"). "Dòng thời gian" for timeline. "Thu nhỏ đến mức xa nhất" for zoom out as far as possible. Check the idea that the universe is so big a town cannot be seen.
read.sections.2.text.source: A wide view helps us see a pattern, which is a change that repeats or goes on for a long time. Maps from many different years can show Riverstone slowly spreading across the river. But a wide view can also hide people, because a line on a timeline cannot show every person's choices. Some historians zoom out as far as possible, to the whole history of the universe. At that scale, one town is far too small to see. That is why historians move between scales. Neither scale is always better, because the best scale depends on the question you ask.
read.sections.2.text.back: A wide view helps us see a pattern, that is, a change that repeats or lasts over a long time. Maps from many different years might show Riverstone slowly spreading to the other side of the river. But a wide view can also hide people, because a line on a timeline cannot show each person's choices. Some historians zoom out as far as possible, to the whole history of the universe. At that scale, a small town is so small it cannot be seen. That is why historians move between scales. No scale is always better, because the best scale depends on the question you ask.

read.sections.2.simpler.source: A wide view shows a pattern. A pattern is a change that goes on for a long time. Maps from many years show the town getting bigger. But a wide view can hide people. A timeline cannot show every person. Some historians look at the whole universe. Then you cannot see one town at all. So historians move from close to wide. The best scale depends on your question.
read.sections.2.simpler.back: A wide view shows a pattern. A pattern is a change that lasts over a long time. Maps from many years show the town slowly getting bigger. But a wide view can hide people. A timeline cannot show each person. Some historians look at the whole universe. Then you cannot even see a town. So historians move from close-up to wide view. The best scale depends on your question.

write.example.note: Check that the example uses the starters in order and reads naturally in the first person.
write.example.source: At the scale of one afternoon, we notice heavy rain and a closed bridge. A trader has to take a longer road, so she arrives late. Over 20 years, the evidence shows a town that is growing. New homes and markets spread to both sides of the river. The close scale helps us answer why one trader was late that day. The wide scale helps us answer why Riverstone built two new bridges. Together, the two scales show that one place can have more than one story.
write.example.back: At the scale of one afternoon, we notice heavy rain and a closed bridge. A merchant had to take a longer detour, so she arrived late. Over 20 years, the evidence shows a growing town. New houses and markets spread to both banks of the river. The narrow scale helps us answer why one merchant arrived late that day. The wide scale helps us answer why Riverstone built two new bridges. Put together, the two scales show that a place can have more than one story.

watch.summary.note: "13,8 tỉ năm" (13.8 billion years) uses the Vietnamese decimal comma and "tỉ" (spelling like "lí"). The sentence "Các nhà khoa học giải thích rằng ..." keeps science framing neutral; check it is respectful to faith accounts (see Lesson 4). | Review: Cosmology (13,8 tỉ năm, 'Big Bang' not named); English says 'scientists explain'. Check that the sentence about the universe's beginning reads as neutral for faith-sensitive families (Lesson 4 follows).
watch.summary.source: This short video uses the widest scale there is: the history of the whole universe. Scientists explain that the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago. At first, it was very small and very hot. Then it grew bigger and cooler. It has kept changing ever since. At this scale, you do not see any person, town or country. You see only very big changes over billions of years. This helps us see that human history is a small part of a much longer story. But this scale cannot tell us why one trader was late, or how one family lived. To learn those things, historians zoom in.
watch.summary.back: This short video uses the widest scale possible: the history of the whole universe. Scientists explain that the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago. At first, it was very small and very hot. Then it grew and cooled. Since then it has always kept changing. At this scale, you cannot see a single person, town or country. You only see very large changes over billions of years. This helps us see that human history is a small part of a much longer story. But this scale does not tell us why a merchant arrived late, or how a family lived. To know those things, historians zoom in.
